raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Standalone FlashInfer all-reduce ignored an explicitly configured cutoff: the
topology-tuned value (or the world-size default) always won, so users could
not raise the routing cutoff on topologies where the default is conservative —
on sm90/TP8 the default standalone cutoff is 0.5 MiB, while FlashInfer MNNVL
outperforms the NCCL path for small decode all-reduces on H200 NVSwitch.

Reviewer feedback on the first version (thanks @GirasoleY) also identified
that reusing the fused-pass `fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb` for standalone
dispatch conflated two settings and could implicitly enable unvalidated
topologies (e.g. TP16 on sm90), and that `get_fi_ar_workspace()` could still
over-allocate the workspace. All three are addressed.

## Changes

- New dedicated pass-config field `fi_allreduce_standalone_max_size_mb`
  (default `None`); standalone all-reduce reads only this field.
  `fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb` keeps its fused-pass meaning.
- One shared cutoff resolution for `FlashInferAllReduce` and
  `get_fi_ar_workspace()`: explicit standalone value → topology-tuned cutoff
  → world-size default. The standalone workspace floor honors the override
  (no over-allocation), while larger caller-provided fused-workspace
  requirements are preserved.
- The explicit override changes the cutoff, never topology support: world
  sizes with neither a tuned standalone cutoff nor a default-table entry
  (e.g. TP16 on sm90) stay disabled and fall back to NCCL.

## End-to-end results (8×H200, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, TP8/EP8)

Fixed 1024-in / 2048-out requests, median output tok/s of 3 rounds per
concurrency, identical flags for both arms (same build; only
`VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` and the override differ):

| Configuration | standalone FI AR off | on, mnnvl + 2 MiB override | Gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| concurrency 16 | 506.7 | 528.8 | +4.4% |
| concurrency 32 | 514.2 | 529.7 | +3.0% |

Ablation with the default 0.5 MiB sm90 cutoff (override unset): 528.5 / 531.9
— the workload-level gain comes from standalone MNNVL all-reduce itself; the
override matters for decode batch shapes above the conservative default
(hidden 7168 × BF16: 37–146-token batches only route to FlashInfer with the
2 MiB cutoff; the boundary is covered by unit + GPU smoke tests). TPOT
unchanged (29.5–30 ms); all requests completed with exact input/output
lengths, zero failures.

TP16 on sm90 (two-node probe, 16 ranks): all ranks stayed disabled, zero
workspace calls, NCCL fallback all-reduce passed — the override cannot enable
an unsupported topology.

## Tests

- `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`: new focused tests for
  standalone/fused arg independence, override precedence over tuning,
  workspace-floor honoring (including the larger-fused-requirement case),
  the 2 MiB routing boundary, and the TP16-on-sm90 guard.
- Focused run: **29 passed, 19 deselected**; `ruff check` + `ruff format`
  clean.

## Usage

```bash
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1 VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=mnnvl \
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fi_allreduce_standalone_max_size_mb": 2}}'
```

Thanks for the review @GirasoleY — all three points are addressed in the force-pushed
commits (rebased onto current `main`; Mergify cleared `needs-rebase`).

**1. `get_fi_ar_workspace()` over-allocation** — fixed. Standalone sizing now
goes through the same cutoff resolution as `FlashInferAllReduce`
(`_get_standalone_workspace_floor`). With an explicit 2 MiB cutoff, hidden
size 7168, BF16, the workspace floor is 146 tokens instead of the tuned size.
Larger caller-provided fused-workspace requirements are still preserved (a
direct request for 512 tokens still creates 512).

**2. Separate arg** — added `fi_allreduce_standalone_max_size_mb`
(`PassConfig`, default `None`). Standalone all-reduce reads only this field;
`fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb` keeps its fused-pass meaning and no longer
leaks into standalone dispatch. Precedence: explicit standalone value →
topology-tuned cutoff → world-size default.

**3. TP16 on sm90** — you were right, the previous version implicitly enabled
it: with an explicit override set, `flashinfer_max_size(16)` returned the
override even though the sm90 default table has no TP16 entry. Fixed by making
the override change only the cutoff, never topology support: world sizes with
neither a tuned standalone cutoff nor a default-table entry stay disabled and
fall back to NCCL. Re-verified on current `main` with a two-node sm90 TP16
probe (2×8 H200, 16 ranks): all ranks stayed disabled under the explicit
2 MiB override with zero workspace calls, the unmocked production path (real
backend resolver) also stayed disabled, and a direct two-node NCCL all-reduce
passed numerics. `test_flashinfer_standalone_override_does_not_enable_tp16_sm90`
locks the guard in.

**Validation on current `main`** (8×H200 NVSwitch, driver 570.133, torch
2.13/cu129, flashinfer 0.7.0):

- Focused distributed tests: **29 passed, 19 deselected** (`-k flashinfer`),
  `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean.
- TP8 real-workspace smoke: explicit 2 MiB override →
  `max_workspace_size = 2097152`, `max_num_tokens = 146` (workspace sized to
  the override, not the tuned/default floor), and `allreduce_fusion` output
  matches a reference NCCL all-reduce exactly; the 147-token probe is
  correctly rejected at the boundary.
- End-to-end A/B, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, TP8/EP8, fixed 1024-in/2048-out,
  median output tok/s of 3 rounds per concurrency, identical flags for both
  arms (same build; only `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` and the override
  differ):

  | Configuration | standalone FI AR off | on, mnnvl + 2 MiB override | Gain |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | concurrency 16 | 506.7 | 528.8 | +4.4% |
  | concurrency 32 | 514.2 | 529.7 | +3.0% |

  An ablation with the default 0.5 MiB sm90 cutoff (override unset, same
  build) lands at 528.5 / 531.9 — i.e. on this workload the gain comes from
  standalone MNNVL all-reduce itself, while the override matters for decode
  batch shapes above the conservative default (hidden 7168 × BF16: batches of
  37–146 tokens route to FlashInfer only with the 2 MiB cutoff; the unit and
  smoke tests verify that routing boundary). All requests completed with
  exact input/output lengths, zero failures; TPOT unchanged (29.5–30 ms).

+def _mock_flashinfer_allreduce_init(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:

Thanks for the review @GirasoleY — all three points are addressed in the force-pushed
commits (rebased onto current `main`; Mergify cleared `needs-rebase`).

**1. `get_fi_ar_workspace()` over-allocation** — fixed. Standalone sizing now
goes through the same cutoff resolution as `FlashInferAllReduce`
(`_get_standalone_workspace_floor`). With an explicit 2 MiB cutoff, hidden
size 7168, BF16, the workspace floor is 146 tokens instead of the tuned size.
Larger caller-provided fused-workspace requirements are still preserved (a
direct request for 512 tokens still creates 512).

**2. Separate arg** — added `fi_allreduce_standalone_max_size_mb`
(`PassConfig`, default `None`). Standalone all-reduce reads only this field;
`fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb` keeps its fused-pass meaning and no longer
leaks into standalone dispatch. Precedence: explicit standalone value →
topology-tuned cutoff → world-size default.

**3. TP16 on sm90** — you were right, the previous version implicitly enabled
it: with an explicit override set, `flashinfer_max_size(16)` returned the
override even though the sm90 default table has no TP16 entry. Fixed by making
the override change only the cutoff, never topology support: world sizes with
neither a tuned standalone cutoff nor a default-table entry stay disabled and
fall back to NCCL. Re-verified on current `main` with a two-node sm90 TP16
probe (2×8 H200, 16 ranks): all ranks stayed disabled under the explicit
2 MiB override with zero workspace calls, the unmocked production path (real
backend resolver) also stayed disabled, and a direct two-node NCCL all-reduce
passed numerics. `test_flashinfer_standalone_override_does_not_enable_tp16_sm90`
locks the guard in.

**Validation on current `main`** (8×H200 NVSwitch, driver 570.133, torch
2.13/cu129, flashinfer 0.7.0):

- Focused distributed tests: **29 passed, 19 deselected** (`-k flashinfer`),
  `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean.
- TP8 real-workspace smoke: explicit 2 MiB override →
  `max_workspace_size = 2097152`, `max_num_tokens = 146` (workspace sized to
  the override, not the tuned/default floor), and `allreduce_fusion` output
  matches a reference NCCL all-reduce exactly; the 147-token probe is
  correctly rejected at the boundary.
- End-to-end A/B, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, TP8/EP8, fixed 1024-in/2048-out,
  median output tok/s of 3 rounds per concurrency, identical flags for both
  arms (same build; only `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` and the override
  differ):

  | Configuration | standalone FI AR off | on, mnnvl + 2 MiB override | Gain |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | concurrency 16 | 506.7 | 528.8 | +4.4% |
  | concurrency 32 | 514.2 | 529.7 | +3.0% |

  An ablation with the default 0.5 MiB sm90 cutoff (override unset, same
  build) lands at 528.5 / 531.9 — i.e. on this workload the gain comes from
  standalone MNNVL all-reduce itself, while the override matters for decode
  batch shapes above the conservative default (hidden 7168 × BF16: batches of
  37–146 tokens route to FlashInfer only with the 2 MiB cutoff; the unit and
  smoke tests verify that routing boundary). All requests completed with
  exact input/output lengths, zero failures; TPOT unchanged (29.5–30 ms).
